# Farely

A personal Android rideshare/delivery driver assistant for Wrocław. It reads the driver's **own**
Bolt / Uber / FreeNow offer cards off-screen through an [[android-accessibility-service]], scores each
one on {{deadhead-adjusted-net-profit}} in PLN, and draws an ACCEPT / MARGINAL / DECLINE bubble over
the ride app. Around that core sit demand-zone positioning, a venue let-out events calendar
({{event-driven-demand-positioning}}), a multi-app "chore" autopilot, and
[[on-device-black-box-diagnostics]].

## The name

The source **folder** is `Farley`; the **product** is `Farely` — fare + *-ly*. Everything inside the
repo spells it Farely: `package.json` `"name": "farely"`, appId and Kotlin package `com.farely.app`,
the README H1, the git remote. "Farley" is a local directory typo only. Wiki `sources:` paths must use
the folder name `Farley/...`; prose uses **Farely**.

## Status — prototype, never field-validated

> "Only the web simulator, never the APK on a live shift."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

Farely has never scored a real offer on a phone in traffic. The web tester (`apps/tester`) was used in
a browser; the Android path stayed unproven. The roadmap board is **accurate about this** — Phase 5
(field testing with real offers) is marked ⚪ not started, and five phases sit at 🟡 "code-complete —
remaining: validate on device". See [[phase-status-board]].

12 commits, `2026-07-12` → `2026-07-25`, all on `main`, no tags, no releases, no CI. A debug APK builds
locally but is `.gitignore`d — nothing is published. The first commit alone is 172 files / 22,151
insertions of already-finished work, and the CHANGELOG documents ten days (07-02 → 07-13) that git
never saw: [[import-finished-work-into-git]] in its textbook form. The 2026-07-24/25 tail
(ToS warning, guides, screenshots, Technology/Skills/License) is [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]].

## Pipeline

Accessibility event (debounced 300 ms, restricted to the four driver packages) → `MultiAppCoordinator`
sees the screen **first** and can `freeze` → `OfferNodeParser` reads fare/km/min off the node tree →
dedup 30 s → bridge into the WebView → `offerFromRaw()` + `scoreOffer()` in TypeScript → `showOverlay`
back over the bridge → `OverlayController` draws the bubble with `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY`
([[accessibility-overlay-over-system-alert-window]]). The whole capture side is
[[accessibility-service-overlay]]; the reading strategy is [[node-tree-read-before-ocr]].

## Findings — documentation vs code

Farely is the sharpest instance of [[documentation-drift]] in the source set.

1. **ML Kit OCR is not shipped.** The README and four docs describe Android ML Kit OCR as the
   on-device recognition engine. `com.google.mlkit:text-recognition` is in **no** `build.gradle`,
   `OcrReader.readNow()` returns `null` behind a `// TODO(Phase 4)`, and `OcrReader.instance` is never
   set. The working on-device reader is the accessibility **node-tree parser**. Confirmed at interview.
2. **The test claim is aspirational.** `README.md:174` says "Tested with Vitest and Playwright."
   There is no test runner, no linter, no typecheck and zero test files; `CONTRIBUTING.md` says so
   outright ("do not invent `npm test`") and SRS §2.5 agrees. Playwright was used only to shoot the
   README screenshots. Interview: *"Aspirational — tests were planned."*
3. **The stale chapter index.** `docs/ocr-overlay/README.md` §5 still reads "Phase 0 —
   Documentation. No native code merged yet", ~13 phases behind `02-roadmap.md`.
4. **The permissions doc disagrees with the manifest** — it lists MediaProjection as required and
   denies `INTERNET`; the manifest declares `INTERNET` and never uses MediaProjection.
5. **`guidelines/Guidelines.md`** is an unmodified Figma Make template placeholder, shipped in a
   "professional repo" commit.

## Privacy posture — precisely

"Runs fully on-device" (README §Privacy, post-2026-07-24 rewrite) is **overstated**. Correct: no
server, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics SDK; persistence is `localStorage` + IndexedDB.
Overstated because **OpenFreeMap map tiles and fueleconomy.gov are unconditional outbound requests**,
and the [[anthropic-messages-api]] vision path exists in shipped code (key-gated, off without a key).
SRS §4.10 lists all six external interfaces honestly and `docs/guides/ANDROID-INSTALL.md` states it
correctly — the README does not. Note the direction of travel: the 2026-07-24 README rewrite demoted
the cloud path from VISION's "a deliberate trade-off I switched on" to "ships off by default", which
made the claim **less** accurate, not more. See [[on-device-first-inference]] and
[[opt-in-cloud-fallback]].

**The identity-check freeze** is corroborated in three independent places — `ID_CHECK_HINTS` in the
coordinator, `frozen` short-circuiting `process()` before any parse or screenshot, and `NOVELTY_HINTS`
deliberately excluding every verification term. But the guarantee is **heuristic, not structural**: a
verification screen containing a novelty word the hint list misses could still be captured. Both facts
belong on the record. Related: [[never-automate-the-accept-tap]],
[[privacy-documented-beside-the-feature]].

**Keys** are entered in Settings and persisted to `localStorage` in plaintext. That is not stated as a
limitation anywhere in the repo.

## Declared-but-unused Android permissions

`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION` and `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` (the OCR path they exist for is a
stub), `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` (the overlay deliberately uses `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY` instead), and
`ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` (no native location code — deadhead uses a simulated `positionRef`).
